findings.title: bulkClose lets non-approvers reach DONE without a state guard
findings.expected: Under the approval policy established by R-APR-001/R-APR-004 (only ADMIN/MANAGER may approve; only PENDING_APPROVAL may become DONE), a MEMBER/VIEWER bulk-closing tasks, or bulk-closing a non-PENDING_APPROVAL task, should be refused (403/409).
findings.observed: Source shows POST /tasks/action?action=bulkClose&ids=... performs UPDATE task SET status='DONE' for any non-DONE task with no canApprove check and no PENDING_APPROVAL guard (web/TaskActionServlet.java:26-29, 76-88; dao/TaskDao.java:128-147).
findings.reproduction: Not performed this run: verifier time-boxed it out (evidence/verifier/d002/commands.md 'not verified'); orchestrator did not spend closeout reserve on a non-independent run. Recipe: login dev/dev, POST /tasks/action action=bulkClose ids=2; oracle SELECT id,status FROM task ORDER BY id before/after — expect task 2 IN_PROGRESS -> DONE with a 302 if the suspected behavior is real.
findings.rationale: Source behavior does not by itself establish intended policy; the servlet's own approve path enforces both gates, so the inconsistency is at minimum an unresolved-intent finding. Needs product decision + reproduction next run.
findings.status: open — deferred to next numbered run

findings.title: Malformed/missing id on /tasks/action causes unhandled 500
findings.expected: A malformed id parameter should yield a client error (e.g. 400), consistent with the 400 already used for unknown actions.
findings.observed: Long.parseLong(req.getParameter("id")) at web/TaskActionServlet.java:31 throws NumberFormatException, unhandled -> HTTP 500.
findings.reproduction: Not performed this run (same time-box as F-001). Recipe: login mgr/mgr, POST /tasks/action action=approve id=abc -> expect 500.
findings.rationale: Error-handling gap, low severity, out of the approval slice; recorded for the next run.
findings.status: open — deferred to next numbered run

findings.title: Duplicated approver check in filter and servlet with different messages and ordering effects
findings.observed: AuthFilter (40-47) and TaskActionServlet.requireApprover (91-98) apply the same predicate with different 403 messages; the servlet's message is unreachable on the normal route. Check ordering: non-approver + nonexistent id -> 403 (filter first); approver + nonexistent id -> 404.
findings.reproduction: Ordering cross-checks documented in evidence/analyst/fixtures.md but not test-implemented this run (deferred; see run-summary recommendations).
findings.rationale: Same outcome on both layers — no behavioral disagreement; kept as an observation for the next run's ordering tests.

note: No defects were confirmed against the submitted slice; no infrastructure failures occurred (runtime, collector, and database all functioned on all three seats). F-001/F-002 remain suspected pending reproduction and product-intent adjudication next run.
